title: The Man Who Stopped a Nuclear War by Doing Nothing
notes: Register: tense but quiet. Do not inflate; the facts are already enormous. Part 4 deliberately complicates 'the man who saved the world': honesty, not undercutting him.

Motion: the bunker beats are tight and building (lamps lighting, counters, the chain of command drawn and cut). The waits (s07, s25, s27, s52) are held completely still: the empty radar scope is the image.
Only one freely licensed photograph of Petrov exists on Commons (p01, 2013, aged 73). Its caption is mandatory: never present it as a 1983 image. In 1983 he is a cartoon in uniform with a vague face.
Both Minuteman photographs carry captions. The launch photograph (p05) must say it is a modern test: nothing was launched in 1983, and the video's whole point depends on that.
Oko satellites are not on Commons. The satellite prop is generic and must never be labelled as Oko or any specific spacecraft.

The bunker, consoles, radar scope and lamps are generic generated objects and rooms. None is presented as Serpukhov-15 itself. The red panel is blank: the word LAUNCH is set as type by the animation layer beside it.
No missiles, explosions or aircraft are drawn. The KAL 007 shootdown is only the real salvage photograph (p04).
Political leaders are not drawn: Andropov appears only in his photograph, Reagan only as type.
Every archival URL was resolved from the Commons API.
Guide object: the black telephone (s05, s06, s56).

petrov.desc: Stanislav Petrov: in 1983 a lieutenant colonel of Soviet air defence, aged 44, in a grey-green uniform shirt and tie, short hair; as a young engineer cadet; and in old age in a cardigan; simple vague face

crowd.desc: extras: Soviet duty officers at consoles in 1983 uniforms, senior officers with heavy shoulder boards, a line of career officers in peaked caps, simple vague faces
